newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up on bargain-hunting in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up on bargain-hunting in thin trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Tuesday in low volume as local players hunted bargains following the last few weeks general trend of slipping prices, brokers said.
The General Index rose 0.35 percent to 1,396.9 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 0.2 percent to 1,988.1 points, according to preliminary figures.
"The rise was due to selective buying of cheap stocks after the recent falling trend," said Hernando Pastor of local brokerage T& J.
Tuesday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 0.41 percent to 4.92 soles on weak volume of 394,000 shares.

Luz del Sur, in which the government sold a 30 percent stake earlier this month, closed down 0.32 percent to 3.10 soles on volume of 393,000 shares. In its placement, the government fixed the sale share price for the electricity distributor at this 3.10 sol mark.
Another electricity distributor, Moyopampa - formerly known as Edegel - rose 4.03 percent to 1.29 soles, on volume of 1.69 million shares.
In 1,197 trades, volume was 54.1 million soles ($21.0 million), but this included a 41 million sol cross-trade within the same brokerage of insurance company Profuturo, brokers said.
